canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across the available usage, factual grounding is framed as the degree to which a model's outputs align with real-world distributions and factual information. The same description also says models may be guided toward outputs grounded in factual information and real-world context, so the construct is used through output alignment to real-world context.

Space of facets. The paper systematizes the concept through a desired-distribution lens: real-world distributions are used for factual grounding, in contrast to equal distributions for social equity.

Space of measurement. No measurement instrument or behavioral indicator is linked to factual grounding. In the available papers, it is presented conceptually rather than tied to a benchmark, human evaluation, LLM-as-a-judge method, probe, or analysis.

Links. The only reported relationship is that factual grounding is related to Social bias. The paper expresses this link by framing bias relative to a desired distribution, equal for social equity and real-world for factual grounding.
